```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`SegreCP` fits CP-rank-constrained tensors using Riemannian gradient descent
(`"rgd"`) or Riemannian Gauss--Newton (`"rgn"`). The same two methods support
tensor decomposition, scalar-on-tensor regression, and tensor-on-tensor
regression. CPCA (`"cpca"`) and HOSVD (`"hosvd"`) are the two spectral starts;
random and user-supplied starts are available as well.

The examples below are small and self-contained. They illustrate the public
API, not the paper's full simulation or real-data protocol. Those larger
experiments have separate reproduction instructions linked at the end.

## CP tensor decomposition and convergence

The observed tensor is a noisy rank-one signal. Its dimensions determine the
dimensions of each recovered component.

```{r decomposition}
library(SegreCP)

set.seed(11)
dims <- c(5L, 6L, 4L)
factors <- lapply(dims, function(p) {
  z <- rnorm(p)
  z / sqrt(sum(z^2))
})
truth_components <- cp_components(
  3, lapply(factors, function(z) matrix(z, ncol = 1L))
)
truth <- reconstruct_cp(truth_components)
observed <- truth + array(rnorm(prod(dims), sd = 0.05), dim = dims)

fit_rgd <- segre_decompose(
  observed, rank = 1L, method = "rgd", init = "cpca",
  control = segre_control(max_iter = 6L), keep_history = TRUE
)
fit_rgn <- segre_decompose(
  observed, rank = 1L, method = "rgn", init = "hosvd",
  control = segre_control(max_iter = 6L), keep_history = TRUE
)
dim(reconstruct_cp(fit_rgn))
cp_relative_error(fit_rgn, truth_components)
```

`convergence_data()` reports the observed least-squares objective at
initialization and after each completed sweep. With a known simulated truth,
it also reports reconstruction error; that oracle error is unavailable on
ordinary data and need not decrease at every sweep.

```{r convergence, fig.width=6.6, fig.height=4.1, fig.cap="Observed objective relative to initialization for the two methods."}
rgd_path <- convergence_data(fit_rgd, truth_components)
rgn_path <- convergence_data(fit_rgn, truth_components)
stopifnot(all(rgd_path$objective_ratio > 0),
          all(rgn_path$objective_ratio > 0))
plot(rgd_path$iteration, rgd_path$objective_ratio, type = "b", log = "y",
     pch = 16, col = "#D55E00", xlab = "Completed sweep",
     ylab = "Observed objective / initial objective")
lines(rgn_path$iteration, rgn_path$objective_ratio, type = "b",
      pch = 17, col = "#0072B2")
legend("topright", c("RGD (CPCA)", "RGN (HOSVD)"),
       col = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2"), pch = c(16, 17),
       lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

An `rTensor::Tensor` can replace the base array at the same API boundary:

```{r rtensor}
tensor_input <- rTensor::as.tensor(observed)
stopifnot(identical(dim(as_segre_array(tensor_input)), dims))
```

## Scalar-on-tensor regression

For regression, rows are observations. A matrix with one vectorized
predictor tensor per row is the most direct representation; an array of
dimensions `c(n, input_dims)` is also accepted.

```{r scalar-regression}
set.seed(12)
n <- 60L
input_dims <- c(3L, 4L)
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * prod(input_dims)), nrow = n)
beta <- 2 * outer(c(1, 0, 0), c(1, 0, 0, 0))
y <- as.numeric(X %*% as.vector(beta) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.05))

fit_scalar <- segre_regress(
  X, y, rank = 1L, input_dims = input_dims,
  method = "rgn", init = "hosvd",
  control = segre_control(max_iter = 5L)
)
dim(coef(fit_scalar))
head(predict(fit_scalar, X), 3L)
```

## Tensor-on-tensor regression

The coefficient tensor uses input modes first, then output modes. In this
example the response has two `2`-dimensional modes.

```{r tensor-regression}
set.seed(13)
n <- 50L
input_dims <- c(2L, 3L)
output_dims <- c(2L, 2L)
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * prod(input_dims)), nrow = n)
beta_factors <- list(c(1, 0), c(1, 0, 0), c(1, 0), c(1, 0))
beta <- array(2 * Reduce(kronecker, rev(beta_factors)),
              dim = c(input_dims, output_dims))
Y <- array(as.numeric(X %*% matrix(beta, nrow = prod(input_dims))) +
             rnorm(n * prod(output_dims), sd = 0.05),
           dim = c(n, output_dims))

fit_tensor <- segre_regress(
  X, Y, rank = 1L, input_dims = input_dims,
  output_dims = output_dims, method = "rgd", init = "cpca",
  control = segre_control(max_iter = 5L)
)
dim(coef(fit_tensor))
dim(predict(fit_tensor, X[1:3, , drop = FALSE]))
```

See `?segre_decompose`, `?segre_regress`, `?cp_initialize`, and
`?segre_control` for inputs, outputs, and numerical controls. The code that
reproduces the simulations and the trade-data analysis of the paper is in the
`reproducibility/` directory of the GitHub repository; the trade data are not
distributed with the package.
